requirement:
Generated coverage-report paths MUST be distinct and MUST be rejected when they
conflict with an existing book chapter.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.test-coverage.index.paths` has two obligations. Generated coverage-report paths MUST be distinct, and they MUST be rejected when they conflict with an existing book chapter. I read `populate_in` only to see which paths it generates: the per-attempt detail path `coverage-reports/{run}-{attempt}.md` and the per-run captured-source path from `fn[source_path]`.

The marked test is `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unavailable_runs_are_readable_and_generated_paths_cannot_collide]`. It covers each obligation and each kind of generated path:

- **Existing chapter vs. attempt report path.** It records one attempt and pushes a `Chapter` at exactly `reports/coverage-reports/{run}-{id}.md`. It asserts that `populate` returns an error containing "conflicts". This covers rejection of an attempt report that conflicts with an existing chapter.
- **Existing chapter vs. captured-source path.** In a fresh fixture it pushes a chapter at `source_path(reports/coverage.md, run.id)`. It asserts the same "conflicts" error. This covers the second kind of generated path.
- **Distinctness among generated paths.** It copies an attempt directory under a new directory name, so two records share the same run and attempt identity. It asserts that `populate` fails with "conflicts" rather than generating the same report path twice. This exercises the `generated.insert` duplicate check.
- **Non-conflicting case.** The first part of the test populates a fixture with no runs and checks that it succeeds. Other tests in the module populate successfully with generated chapters, so the non-conflict path is not left untested.

A source path cannot collide with an attempt path, because the attempt id must be a UUID and so can't be the literal "source". Per-run source pages are deduplicated by run id before their paths are checked. No further distinctness scenario follows from the text.

The assertions check for an error whose message contains "conflicts". That message is specific to these checks, so the assertions would fail if the implementation silently accepted a collision. I found no gap in the obligations the subject states.
